xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4561: Upgrade the dashboard to React 19 and enable the React Compiler with a no-manual-memo ratchet

plan.title: Upgrade the dashboard to React 19 and enable the React Compiler with a no-manual-memo ratchet
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

metadata.sizeJustification: The plan names about 34 files across 13 path prefixes, but most are one-line edits: 8 React 19 type fixes, 3 Vite/Vitest config lines, 3 package.json files plus bun.lock, and docs. The burn-down that would make the issue large (159 skipped files, about 200 files of manual memo) is already split into six sibling issues by WI-11. What remains cannot be split further. The coverage test and its baseline only mean something once the compiler is on with the exact pinned toolchain, and the before/after timings bracket the React upgrade and the compiler switch together (PAN-4560 precedent). The three ratchets and the ratchet audit share the same baseline-file contract. Every item is still its own commit with its own Item: trailer and its own test.

narratives.Problem: The dashboard frontend memoizes by hand: 404 useMemo and 532 useCallback call lines, plus 12 memo() wrappers, across 1,208 source files. It runs React 18, and the React Compiler's output targets React 19. Nothing stops new manual memo, and nothing reports components the compiler skips. A planning probe with oxc-transform-react@0.152.0 found 159 files with 345 compiler diagnostics today. eslint-plugin-react-hooks@7.1.1 finds rule violations in 165 files.
narratives.Proposal: Upgrade the frontend and apps/mobile to React 19.3 and fix the 8 resulting type errors. Move visx to 4.0.0. Enable the oxc React Compiler natively through @vitejs/plugin-react 6.1.2 react({ compiler }), with options shared by Vite, Vitest and the phone app in one module. Add three shrink-only ratchets with baselines created in this PR: a Vitest coverage test that compiles every frontend source file and fails on any new or raised skip (diagnostics plus 'use no memo' directives) or any stale row; a lint step that counts useMemo/useCallback/memo call sites per file; and the eslint-plugin-react-hooks compiler rules with a per-file allowlist. Extend lint-ratchet-audit.sh to cover them. Record before and after dev cold-start and vite build timings on the issue, document the rules, and file six sibling burn-down issues by directory.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Fixing any currently skipped file, including the App.tsx route split (sibling issues do this)
- Removing any existing useMemo, useCallback or memo
- Adopting new React 19 APIs (use, actions, ref as a prop, <Context> as provider)
- Ratcheting apps/mobile/src's own source
- Turning on react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
- Moving ESLint to v9 or flat config
- Upgrading zustand or any dependency not named in the PRD
- Adding babel-plugin-react-compiler or @rolldown/plugin-babel to any build or test pipeline
- Failing the build on a compiler diagnostic (panicThreshold stays 'none')
- Editing the OKF knowledge bundle

autoDecisions.summary: AC 3 ('a test fails when the compiler skips any file') is met as a shrink-only ratchet. The test fails on any skip in a file without a baseline row, on a raised count and on a stale row, and the 159 currently skipped files are baselined.
autoDecisions.rationale: Fixing 159 files across about 50 directories, plus manual-memo removal in about 200 files, is far beyond one reviewable PR and the finalize size limits. The issue title says 'ratchet' and Proposal step 4 says 'file by file'. The ratchet makes new skips impossible from the day it lands, and WI-11 files the burn-down as six sibling issues.

autoDecisions.summary: Pin @vitejs/plugin-react exactly to 6.1.2 and oxc-transform-react exactly to 0.152.0.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue asks for the latest 6.1.x. 6.1.2's peer range is oxc-transform-react ^0.152.0. A probe with 0.156.0 (the newest 6.3.0 accepts) gave the same diagnostics (161 files versus 159). Exact pins keep the skip baseline reproducible between machines.

autoDecisions.summary: React and react-dom ^19.3.1, @types/react and @types/react-dom ^19.3.0, in both the frontend and apps/mobile.
autoDecisions.rationale: These are the newest releases that are at least two weeks old. apps/mobile imports frontend source and dedupes React, so both must share the React major.

visx 3.12 is the only React dependency whose peer range stops at React 18. 4.0.0 (2026-06) declares React 19. The frontend's ambient.d.ts already types these modules, and only two GodView components use them.

autoDecisions.summary: Enable the compiler in vitest.config.ts and apps/mobile/vite.config.ts too, through one shared options module.
autoDecisions.rationale: Tests must exercise what ships. A shared object keeps the coverage scan, the build and the tests from drifting. If a test fails only when compiled, the component is fixed; the fallback is a single 'use no memo' plus a baseline raise named in the PR.

autoDecisions.summary: oxc (the build's compiler) is the authority for skipped files. eslint-plugin-react-hooks gets its own file allowlist, and exhaustive-deps stays off.
autoDecisions.rationale: The ESLint plugin's Babel compiler disagrees with oxc on 84 files and adds lint-only rules. exhaustive-deps would warn on hundreds of existing effects.

autoDecisions.summary: The manual-memo check is a count-per-file ratchet script in the lint chain, not an ESLint rule.
autoDecisions.rationale: Lint runs with --no-inline-config, so ESLint cannot exempt lines. A per-file ESLint exemption would let new memo calls into the 200 files that already have one.

autoDecisions.summary: Timings: 'before' at the branch base (React 18, no compiler), 'after' at the end. Medians of 3. vite build alone, without tsc. Dev cold start = vite spawn with an empty .vite cache until #root has a child in headless Chromium.
autoDecisions.rationale: This brackets the two changes the issue asks about and isolates the compiler transform cost from type checking.

autoDecisions.summary: Burn-down is six sibling issues, split by directory, each covering skip fixes, lint allowlist entries and memo removal for its paths.
autoDecisions.rationale: Directory groups are independent and reviewable. Combining skip fixes and memo removal per directory enforces the ordering rule (remove memo only after a file compiles).
